name: The Bunya Pine of Manly West

location.address: Road reserve, Manly Road, Manly West (adjacent to 29 Whatmore Place)

access: Free, stands on a public road reserve alongside Manly Road
transport: No station in Manly West itself; about 35-40 minutes from central Brisbane by train and bus, further out than this city's other trees
verify_notes: Was a standing lead in data/leads/brisbane.json ('The Bunya Tree of Manly West'). Brisbane Heritage Register (heritage.brisbane.qld.gov.au/heritage-places/1024, directly fetched) is the one source naming the tree itself: planted 1891 by John Hargreaves at the entrance to his farm and canning factory, the sole survivor of the original planting, coordinates -27.474671,153.158523. A second, independent source (queenslandplaces.com.au/manly-west, directly fetched) corroborates the surrounding history (Hargreaves acquired the Woondall property, established a cannery, major local employer) but does not name the tree or the 1891 date, so the tree-specific facts rest on the heritage register alone; the story says so plainly, matching the precedent already shipped as bne_020 (Fig Tree of Haig Road, single-sourced, flagged). Distance from CBD (~14km, ~35-40 min by train/bus) exceeds the ~30 minute day-trip guideline; included per the Blarney-for-Cork/Fota-for-Cork precedent, labeled honestly with the real travel time rather than excluded. Age: register's 'approximately 110 years old when documented' (citation dated 2005-2006) plus years since gives roughly 135 today; carried as a band (125-145) rather than a precise figure.
